Build me a vast, abandoned stone city in a rugged mountain valley, with a pale turquoise, fast-flowing river winding through the settlement and dividing dense districts of ruins on both banks. Arrange dozens upon dozens of roofless medieval buildings organically along narrow dirt lanes, irregular courtyards, and stepped rocky ground, clustering them most tightly beside the river and thinning them toward the surrounding slopes. Use weathered gray masonry throughout: squat rectangular houses, taller blocky halls, broken towers, and several larger Gothic structures with pointed and rounded arches, arcades, buttress-like wall sections, and partially collapsed upper stories. Most buildings should retain only jagged exterior walls and exposed room divisions, while a few include decayed timber frames, beams, balconies, or skeletal roofs. Connect the banks with a narrow arched stone bridge, and place scattered stairs, retaining walls, rubble piles, fallen logs, and isolated masonry fragments among the ruins. Shape the terrain as uneven brown earth broken by broad rock shelves, cliffs, large pale boulders, gullies, and steep ridges that enclose the valley. Populate open spaces and settlement edges with irregular clusters of mature leafy trees, sparse woodland, scrub, grasses, weeds, and small wildflowers, leaving a few broad bare courtyards amid the denser blocks. Beyond the city, continue into rocky, lightly forested mountains, with low white clouds and mist threading between slopes and buildings. Keep the layout sprawling, tightly packed, and distinctly unordered, with architecture conforming to the natural rock rather than a grid, and give the scene a quiet, hazy, overgrown atmosphere under soft daylight.
